newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican TV plans may be altered by delay in talks.
newsitem.headline: Mexican TV plans may be altered by delay in talks.

text.p: If the international satellite protocols for direct-to-home (DTH) television in Mexico were not established by the end of the year, DTH companies might be forced to use Mexican satellites, the chief of Mexico's Federal Telecommunications Commission said Friday.

"They haven't been signed yet," Carlos Casasus, president of the commission, told Mexican legislators. "They are very complicated legal agreements, very complicated documents, with very relevant implications for the future."
Casasus said companies that do not need to transmit their signals on foreign satellites can begin using services on Mexican satellites.
For example, Grupo Televisa SA de CV will be able to use its Mexican satellites until protocols are signed, he said.
But stalled negotiations with the United States over satellite protocols has delayed the service for the Mexican firm Multivision, which will depend on U.S. satellites.
